title: Revised Surface Treatment and Sealing Practice for Aluminium Lower Shell Lap Joints

issue.reason: Issue B. Earlier issues are not held in this dataset.

abstract: New surface treatment and sealing practice for aluminium lap joints in the lower shell, written after filiform corrosion was found under the paint film at the joint land on aircraft operating in humid coastal environments.

sections.reason: Filiform corrosion under the paint film at the lower shell lap joint land was reported by seven operators, all of them based in humid coastal environments, with the earliest finding at four years in service. Forty-one findings were recorded across the fleet in three years and eleven of them went past the blend-out limit and needed an engineering disposition. The mechanism was traced to the surface treatment being applied outside its stated window on the joining station rather than to the treatment itself, and to a sealing practice that left a capillary path at the fastener head.
sections.description: The practice replaces the single-stage treatment at the lap joint land with a two-stage treatment and fixes the sequence between abrasion, treatment and sealing. The shear tie D5120110715725 and the strap D5120111806797 are re-issued at the new treatment standard, the bracket D5120118402300 gains a sealed edge at the joint land, and the corrosion removal angle D5120120637267 is used where a finding has to be blended before treatment. The edging grommet AES445369-54 is installed at every cable pass-through crossing the treated land, because the earlier grommet trapped moisture against the treatment. Work is at the lower shell in the cargo compartment zones 131 and 141 and the belly fairing zone 191. The practice text is on drawings D51201114548 and D51201185443.
sections.effects: Mass increase of 0.2 kg per aircraft from the additional sealing. No electrical load change. Fully interchangeable, since the change is a process rather than a part. The scheduled detailed visual inspection of the joint land can be extended from four thousand to eight thousand flight cycles once the practice is embodied and recorded. Repair manual content changes in two places: the allowable damage limits for blend-out at the land, and the treatment called out in every metallic repair on the lower shell.
sections.embodiment_note: There is no production cut-in because the joining station process was corrected separately under a manufacturing instruction. Retrofit is by Service Bulletin CRN-51-2001, which is written as an inspect-and-treat action at the next heavy check rather than as a fixed campaign, with the aircraft in the hangar for two shifts.

type_data.production_impact: No cut-in; the joining station sequence was corrected under a separate manufacturing instruction
